clue.text: Overture to Mozart opera with new set is very intimate

parts.note: the opening word of the title of Mozart's opera Cosi fan tutte

indicators.note: new signals that the letters of set are made afresh in another order

explanation.surface: A music lover's cosy evening: a Mozart overture and a fresh stage set.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Overture' is not the music before the curtain but the opening word of the opera's title; 'new' is the anagram signal for the set.
explanation.definitionFit: Superlative of cosy, meaning snug and close, so most intimate.

clue.text: Decisive in a shoemaker

parts.note: a crisp manner is brisk and decisive

explanation.surface: A cobbler with a firm, no-nonsense manner.
explanation.walkthrough: St Crispin is the patron saint of shoemakers and was himself one.
explanation.definitionFit: Saint Crispin, a Roman-era martyr, worked as a cobbler and is the patron of the trade.

clue.text: Fallen angel encompasses the awful ruin of a god

indicators.note: encompasses means the fallen angel's name surrounds the other letters

parts.note: Satan is the angel who fell from heaven

indicators.note: awful signals the letters of ruin are badly jumbled

explanation.surface: The Devil brings dreadful destruction upon a deity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awful' is the anagram signal on ruin, and 'encompasses' puts the shuffled letters inside the fallen angel; 'the' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Saturnian is the adjective relating to the Roman deity Saturn.

clue.text: Two points a girl has to follow

parts.note: E and N are two compass points, east and north
Sue is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A young woman must obey a couple of instructions.
explanation.definitionFit: To ensue is to come afterwards or result, so to come next.

clue.text: Striking musician somehow taps in time endlessly

indicators.note: endlessly means the word time loses its final letter
somehow says the letters of taps in are rearranged in some way

explanation.surface: A percussionist somehow taps along in time, without stopping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts TIME to TIM; 'somehow' turns TAPS IN into PANIST.
explanation.definitionFit: A kettle-drum player strikes the drums with sticks.

clue.text: Bill North uses the back door

parts.note: a bill is a printed notice stuck on a wall, a poster

explanation.surface: Someone named Bill, heading north, sneaks out by the back door.
explanation.definitionFit: A postern is a small rear or side gate of a castle or house.

clue.text: Open award.

definitions.meaning: to force open with a lever

explanation.definitionFit: To prise a lid is to lever it open, and a trophy or reward is also called this.

clue.text: One who cleanses, i.e. a follower of 27

parts.note: sc., short for Latin scilicet, means namely, just as i.e. does
clue 27 is the goddess of vengeance, so her follower is one who takes revenge

explanation.surface: A street cleaner who follows in the wake of the clue twenty-seven goddess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'i.e.' gives SC, the abbreviation for scilicet, 'namely'; 27 across is the goddess of retribution, followed by an avenger.
explanation.definitionFit: Historically a street-cleaner was so called; animals that eat carrion also clear up waste.

clue.text: Ordain in play

definitions.meaning: to decree, as a law or statute is passed
to act out a part on stage

explanation.definitionFit: Parliament makes laws this way, and actors perform roles this way too.

clue.text: Outside left required to be prodded into action

indicators.note: outside means the word for required goes around the letter for left

parts.note: needed means required

explanation.surface: A footballer on the outside left had to be spurred on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outside left' looks like the football position, but 'Outside' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Needled means goaded or provoked into doing something.

clue.text: Stress is cut after a move

indicators.note: after a move says the letters of is cut have been shifted around into a new order

explanation.surface: A chess player feels the strain once a move has been made.
explanation.definitionFit: In prosody an ictus is the beat or accent falling on a syllable.

clue.text: Girl given a farewell in London

parts.note: a maid is an old word for a girl
vale is Latin for goodbye

explanation.surface: A young woman bids someone goodbye somewhere in the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: MAIDA VALE is a residential district of north-west London; the definition is just the hint of place, 'in London'.
explanation.definitionFit: A named district of the English capital, so a place found within that city.

clue.text: Drink time — get the carriage!

parts.note: porter is a dark beer
an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: Drinking time is over, someone calls for their coach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carriage' looks like a horse-drawn coach but means the carrying of goods, or its charge.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words name the transport of goods or luggage and the fee charged for it.

clue.text: Laud's former fortune replaced

definitions.note: read as Laud is: the definition is the verb laud, praise

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife

indicators.note: replaced means the letters of lot are put back in a different order

parts.note: your lot is your fortune or fate

explanation.surface: Archbishop Laud's earlier wealth has been exchanged for something else.
explanation.walkthrough: William Laud was a 17th-century Archbishop of Canterbury; here the name is just the verb 'laud', with 's as 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: To laud is to praise highly, which is exactly what extolling does.

clue.text: Innocent one in church body

indicators.note: in places the letter for one inside the word for the church body

parts.note: the nave is the main body of a church
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A guiltless person sits among the congregation in church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'church body' suggests a governing council, but it is the main hall of the building.
explanation.definitionFit: Naive means unworldly and guileless, a synonym of innocent.

clue.text: They are not wanted if white or pink

definitions.text: They are not wanted if white or pink

parts.words: They are not wanted if white or pink
parts.note: a white one is a costly unwanted possession, and pink ones are drunken hallucinations

explanation.definitionFit: White ones are burdensome gifts and pink ones are seen by drunkards, so neither large beast is welcome.

clue.text: Cross with daughter about dress getting soaked

indicators.note: about means the angry word goes around the word for dress

parts.note: cross means angry, irate
rig is clothing, as in rig-out

explanation.surface: A parent angry with their daughter over an outfit that got drenched.
explanation.definitionFit: Irrigated land has been watered, so it has been drenched or supplied with water.

clue.text: Poem, not so much like prose

parts.note: a rhyme is a short poem
less means not so much

explanation.surface: A poem that reads less like verse and more like prose.
explanation.definitionFit: Prose lacks verse endings that chime, so it is without them.

clue.text: Train sent out, not stopping

indicators.note: out signals the letters of train sent are put out of order

explanation.surface: An express train was dispatched that does not call at stations.
explanation.definitionFit: Transient means passing through briefly rather than staying.

clue.text: Carry on about a Frenchman in a sarcastic way

indicators.note: about means the word for carry on wraps round the French phrase

parts.note: to ply a trade is to carry it on
un is French for a, and a gent is a man

explanation.surface: A Frenchman's conduct is commented on with biting wit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a Frenchman' splits as French 'un' for 'a' plus GENT for 'man'.
explanation.definitionFit: Pungent remarks are sharp and caustic, so pungently means bitingly or cuttingly.

clue.text: Model and dad continue joking

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father
to rag on is to keep teasing

explanation.surface: A fashion model and her father carry on with their banter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Model' is not a catwalk model but a perfect example.
explanation.definitionFit: A paragon is a perfect example, a model of excellence.

clue.text: Right about a Scot being cheerful

indicators.note: about means the abbreviation for right goes around the name

parts.note: Ian is a typically Scottish first name

explanation.surface: A Scotsman in good spirits because he was proved right.
explanation.definitionFit: Riant, from French, means laughing or merry, a synonym of cheerful.

clue.text: Curiously rare metal about in this land

indicators.note: about means the word for metal goes around the other letters

parts.note: tin is a metallic element

indicators.note: curiously signals the letters of rare are oddly arranged

explanation.surface: A scarce metal is found here and there across this country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Curiously' turns RARE into ERRA, which TIN goes 'about'.
explanation.definitionFit: Terrain means a stretch of ground and its physical features.

clue.text: Rule in India with a hard local dignitary

parts.note: the Raj was British rule in India
H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: Under colonial rule in India, a stern local official holds sway.
explanation.definitionFit: A rajah was an Indian prince or ruler, a person of rank in his region.

clue.text: Scots sweetheart has a drink in a large bowl

parts.note: jo is a Scottish word for a sweetheart, as in Burns's John Anderson, my jo
rum is a spirit

explanation.surface: A Scottish lover drinks from a big bowl.
explanation.definitionFit: A jorum is a large drinking vessel or bowl, often for punch.

clue.text: Before or after the cowards find one to go in front

indicators.note: after places the word or behind the word for cowards

parts.note: pre- is the prefix meaning before
curs are contemptible people, cowards

explanation.surface: Whether earlier or later, the cowards pick someone to lead the way.
explanation.definitionFit: A forerunner is someone who comes before and leads the way.

clue.text: Supports — necessities in staging plays

definitions.meaning: things that hold up a structure
the movable objects used by actors on stage

explanation.surface: Stage furniture keeps a theatre production upright.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for properties, stage objects; also struts holding something up.

clue.text: Extremist who helped to assault Rasputin.

indicators.note: helped to says the letters help make up the words assault Rasputin, sitting inside them

explanation.surface: A fanatic who joined in the attack on the Russian mystic Rasputin.
explanation.walkthrough: Rasputin was murdered in 1916 by Russian nobles, which gives the surface its plausibility.
explanation.definitionFit: An ultra is someone with extreme political views.

clue.text: Ear-ring shapes are in gold

indicators.note: shapes means the letters of are in gold are formed into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Earrings come in many shapes, all made of gold.
explanation.definitionFit: A girandole is an ornate pendant earring, often with smaller stones round a large one.

clue.text: The bread-and-butter letter

parts.note: a bread-and-butter letter is a thank-you note, and ta is British slang for thanks

explanation.surface: The classic thank-you note written after staying with someone.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'bread-and-butter letter' is a thank-you note to a host; TA is British informal 'thanks'.
explanation.definitionFit: Theta is the eighth character of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Retributive justice from the daughter of Knox, we hear

definitions.meaning: punishment that is deserved and inevitable

definitions.text: the daughter of Knox, we hear
definitions.meaning: in Greek myth the goddess of vengeance was a daughter of Nyx, Night, whose name sounds like Knox

explanation.surface: Divine punishment comes from the offspring of the Scottish reformer John Knox.
explanation.walkthrough: John Knox suggests Scotland's stern reformer; the sound gives Nyx, the Greek goddess of night.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek goddess of retribution gave her name to any just and inescapable downfall.

clue.text: Fight and beat a tough guy

parts.note: to spar is to box or fight
to tan someone's hide is to beat them

explanation.surface: A boxer brawls with and thrashes a hard man.
explanation.definitionFit: Citizens of ancient Sparta were famed for hardiness and austerity, so the word names a hardy person.
